exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly relates to bypassing or insufficiently enforcing network boundary controls between the DMZ and internal zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient ingress filtering can allow adversaries to use alternative protocols to move data or commands across the DMZ boundary.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted egress allows attackers to reach and exploit remote services on backend tiers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Software Deployment Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers abuse software deployment tools to propagate laterally across systems within the same boundary zone.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Trusted Relationship
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared service accounts propagate implicit trust relationships that adversaries can exploit to move between systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared service account tokens can be stolen and reused to impersonate trusted identities across boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Signaling
exploitedBy.relevance: Monitoring gaps enable covert traffic signaling techniques to operate undetected at the boundary.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Non-isolated management plane ingress exposes remote service interfaces to unauthorized access from untrusted networks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Management interfaces exposed without isolation can be directly exploited by external adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Certificate trust misconfigurations between zones enable adversaries to intercept and manipulate inter-zone traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured certificate trust allows attackers to forge or misuse digital certificates to impersonate trusted zone endpoints.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS is a commonly abused outbound protocol for covert data exfiltration when egress filtering is insufficient.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Permitted HTTP egress channels are leveraged to exfiltrate data via web services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Publish/Subscribe Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries abuse allowed publish/subscribe middleware protocols to bypass zone boundary controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Layer Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Permitted middleware application layer protocols are exploited to traverse zone boundaries covertly.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Fallback Channels
exploitedBy.relevance: Redundant paths with weaker enforcement can serve as fallback channels for adversarial communication.
